questions.prompt: Explain the difference between open and public access levels in Swift. When would you choose open over public? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that public allows external access but prevents subclassing and overriding outside the module
Explains that open allows external subclassing and overriding, chosen when designing reusable framework extension points

questions.modelAnswer: Both open and public allow code to be accessed from outside the defining module. However, open allows external modules to subclass a class or override a method, while public forbids external subclassing and overriding. You choose open when you are designing a framework and intentionally want clients to customize behavior through inheritance.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: Access Control

questions.prompt: What does private(set) do in Swift, and why is it preferred over declaring a property completely private with a separate getter method? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that private(set) provides read access at the enclosing level while restricting writes to private
Explains that it avoids boilerplate getter methods and protects state while keeping standard dot syntax for reading

questions.modelAnswer: The private(set) modifier keeps write access private while allowing read access at the enclosing declaration's access level. It is preferred because it avoids writing boilerplate getter methods while protecting internal state from accidental external modification. External code can read the property with standard dot syntax without being able to mutate it.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: Access Control

questions.prompt: Why does the Swift compiler not synthesize a public memberwise initializer for public structs? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that default memberwise initializers are internal to prevent accidental leakage of private properties
Mentions API stability or protecting external consumers when internal struct properties change

questions.modelAnswer: The Swift compiler creates an internal memberwise initializer by default so internal implementation details are not exposed accidentally. If a public memberwise initializer were generated automatically, adding a private stored property later would break external client code. Requiring an explicit public initializer forces library authors to design a stable API contract intentionally.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: Access Control

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between private and fileprivate access levels in Swift, including how extensions in the same file behave. Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that private is scoped to the enclosing declaration and same-file extensions
Explains that fileprivate is accessible anywhere within the source file, including unrelated types

questions.modelAnswer: The private modifier restricts access to the enclosing type declaration and its extensions within the same source file. The fileprivate modifier allows access from any code anywhere within the same source file, even outside the type declaration. In modern Swift, both private and fileprivate allow same-file extensions to access members, but fileprivate also exposes them to unrelated types in that file.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: Access Control

questions.prompt: What is package access level introduced in Swift 5.9, and what problem does it solve for modular iOS apps? Answer in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that package access shares code across targets inside the same Swift package
Explains that it prevents exposing internal architecture APIs publicly to external clients

questions.modelAnswer: The package access level allows types and members to be shared across multiple targets within the same Swift package. Before package access, sharing code across targets required marking APIs public, which unintentionally exposed them to external app clients. Package access solves this by keeping modular code internal to the package while enabling collaboration across its internal modules.
